The core insight is that goal-oriented behavior can be decomposed into a graded hierarchy of readinesses, where each level serves as a probabilistic stepping stone toward the ultimate objective. This yields a compositional algebra of behavioral dispositions: the readiness to pursue a secondary resource (like food) is the product of its efficacy at achieving the primary goal (satisfaction) and the strength of that primary demand. Furthermore, the system adapts by updating these readiness values based on empirical feedback about whether the intermediate action actually leads to success, thereby implementing a form of "operational truth" that guides future choices.
